title: Optimize quant kernels: INT8/FP8 smoothquant + dequant fusion
author: Ava Chen
release_notes: Improved INT8 and FP8 quantized inference kernels with smoothquant support and fused dequant+matmul path. Reduced median latency and improved throughput for quantized models; safe fallback to FP16 when kernel unsupported.
description:
Context and motivation:
We observed that quantized inference (INT8 and FP8) paths for common transformer blocks were still paying significant overhead on dequantization and data-layout conversions, which reduces the latency/throughput benefits of quantization in production. This PR implements a fused dequant+matmul kernel, smoothquant scaling integration, and scheduler-level micro-batching optimizations to expose real-world perf wins for inference workloads.

What this PR changes:
- New fused kernel: dequantize + GEMM (int8->FP16/FP32 internal accumulation) implemented for NVIDIA GPUs (CUDA) and selected CPU fallbacks. The kernel minimizes memory copies and eliminates an intermediate unpack buffer in the hot path.
- FP8 support: optimized FP8 (E4M3) matmul path with improved accumulation and overflow handling; added quantization helpers for runtime selection between FP8/INT8/FP16 based on model profile.
- SmoothQuant integration: added per-channel scaling logic during weight layout transform so that smoothquant scaling factors are baked into the quantized weight layout at compile time; no extra scaling at runtime.
- Dequant fusion path: compiler/runtime now emits an alternate operator graph for blocks that can use fused dequant+matmul, avoiding standalone dequant ops in the plan.
- Scheduler + batching: continuous-batching scheduler tweaks to prefer larger micro-batches for quantized kernels where latency/throughput curve is favorable; introduced a minimal warm-up micro-batch to populate KV cache in a quant-friendly layout.
- Fallbacks and safety: when fused kernel is not available for a model/hardware combo, the runtime falls back to existing dequant + matmul path. Added runtime checks and a telemetry flag to detect numeric regression.

Performance (end-to-end, measured on H100 / A100 in our perf-lab):
- INT8: median latency -12%, p95 -18%, throughput +22% on 8k-token batches for LLaMA-2-13B-ish profile.
- FP8 (E4M3): median latency -9%, p95 -14%, throughput +16% on same profile.
- Combined smoothquant + fused dequant path: additional ~3-5% improvement over naive quantization because scaling is applied at layout-time.

Testing and validation:
- Unit tests added for quant helpers, fused kernel wrapper, and scheduler heuristics.
- Integration tests: end-to-end text generation smoke tests across INT8/FP8/FP16 codepaths.
- Perf harness: reproducible bench runs captured in benchmark-lab with CI tags.
- Canary rollout: staged canary on Dedicated GPUs with telemetry to monitor output distribution and latency regressions.

Rollout plan:
- Initial rollout on dedicated clusters with opt-in flag for customers (disabled by default for hosted until further A/B).
- Monitor numeric drift; if telemetry shows output quality regression > threshold, automatically revert to FP16 path for that route.

Checklist:
- [x] Implement fused dequant+matmul kernel (CUDA)
- [x] Add FP8 fast path and quant selection logic
- [x] Integrate smoothquant into weight transformation pipeline
- [x] Scheduler micro-batching improvements and KV warm-up flow
- [x] Unit/integration tests
- [x] Benchmarks and canary rollout plan

References:
- Linear: ENG-2418 (quant kernel roadmap), ENG-2470 (scheduler batching improvements)
- Internal benchmark runs: benchmark-lab/quant-fusion/2026-02-20

Notes:
- This change touches low-level kernels and scheduler logic; reviewers should pay attention to numeric edge cases (overflow in FP8 accumulation) and the telemetry instrumentation for silent fallbacks.
